chunks: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'ah from Abdullah ibn Jabala from Ibn Bukayr from Ubayd ibn Zurara from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The divorce of the sick person is valid, and his marriage is valid.
ai.seo_question: Is the divorce of a sick person valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies that a sick man retains full legal capacity (ahliyyah) for both contracting marriage and effecting divorce, countering potential assumptions that illness might impair such juridical acts. In Shia jurisprudence, this establishes that unless the illness causes a specific loss of sanity or consent, the individual's marital status remains fully actionable. This ruling underscores the principle that physical ailment, distinct from mental incapacity, does not suspend one's legal agency in family law matters.

en.hubeali:
Humeyd Bin Ziyad, from Ibn sama’at, from Abdullah Bin Jabala, from Ibn Bukeyr, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The divorce of the sick (man) is not allowed, but his marriage is allowed’.
en.sarwar: 4. Humayd ibn Ziyad has narrated from ibn Sama‘ah from ‘Abd Allah ibn Jabalah from ibn Bukayr from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurarah who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One’s divorcing during his illness is not permissible, however, his marriage is permissible.’”
